title: Convex subgroup chains are bounded by rational rank
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a totally ordered abelian group, such as the value group attached to a valuation ring of a field [def-weil-field], and put $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)=\dim_{\mathbf Q}(\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)$ [def-trf-rational-rank], with cardinal-valued dimension. If $H_0\subsetneq H_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq H_n$ is a strict chain of convex subgroups of $\Gamma$ (a subgroup $H$ is convex when $h_1,h_2\in H$ and $h_1\le x\le h_2$ imply $x\in H$), then $\operatorname{Cardinal.mk}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)\le\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)$.

source.place: §2.1, pp. 7–8, the convex-rank/height consequence of the value-group correspondence, checked alongside Lemma 2.1.2 and Corollary 2.1.3(i) in the author’s v3 PDF online at https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Stable_Modification.pdf.

proof.text: If n=0 there is nothing to prove. Assume n>0. For each i=1,…,n choose an element x_i∈H_i\H_{i-1}; replacing x_i by -x_i when necessary, assume x_i>0. This is possible because each strict inclusion supplies a nonzero element and a totally ordered abelian group lets us choose one of an element and its negative that is positive.

source.place: Temkin §2.1, pp. 7–8, convex-rank discussion; the element-selection argument is written out here.

proof.text: The ordered group Γ is torsion-free: if m>0 and mγ=0, then a nonzero γ may be replaced by -γ>0, which gives 0<mγ, a contradiction. More generally, if H is convex, x>0, and m x∈H for some m>0, then 0≤x≤m x and convexity forces x∈H. Thus the image of every x_i in the quotient H_i/H_{i-1} has infinite order.

source.place: Temkin §2.1, pp. 7–8, convex-subgroup argument; the torsion-free and convexity details are written out here.

proof.text: The tensors x_1⊗ 1,…,x_n⊗ 1 are linearly independent over ℚ. Indeed, suppose ∑_i q_i(x_i⊗ 1)=0 with q_i∈ℚ. Clearing denominators gives an integer relation ∑_i a_i x_i=0; because Γ has no nonzero finite-order element, the cited torsion-free rationalization lemma gives injectivity of Γ→Γ⊗_ℤℚ, so this reduction loses no information. If j is the largest index with a_j≠0, then −a_jx_j=∑_{i<j}a_i x_i∈H_{j-1}. Replacing signs if needed, the preceding convexity observation applied to |a_j|x_j forces x_j∈H_{j-1}, contradicting its choice. Hence all a_i, and therefore all q_i, vanish.

source.place: Temkin §2.1, pp. 7–8, the convex-rank bound; the linear-independence proof is written out here.

proof.text: By the definition of rational rank, $\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ is a $\mathbf Q$-vector space whose cardinal dimension is $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)$. Step 3 gives a linearly independent family indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, so [lem-trf-independent-family-cardinal-dimension] shows that its cardinality $\operatorname{Cardinal.mk}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)$ is at most the cardinal dimension of that vector space. Therefore $\operatorname{Cardinal.mk}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)\le\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma)$.

source.place: Temkin §2.1, pp. 7–8, definition of rational rank and convex-rank consequence.
